notes: Test split IDENTICAL to train_xgboost.py's (same random_state=42, test_size=0.2, stratify=label, unmodified row order) - verified matching test-set label distribution before training. Trained on combined_text (decoded path+query_params+body), same text XGBoost's engineered stats are derived from (extract_features.py's build_combined_text()). KNOWN LIMITATION: several classes are defined by a fixed vulnerable endpoint string (cmdi, path_traversal, ssrf); the CNN may partly learn endpoint-matching as a shortcut rather than injected-payload syntax - see module docstring. ABLATION FINDING (payload-only, no endpoint path): test macro F1 dropped to 0.8121 (from 0.9933) and weighted F1 to 0.6445 (from 0.9960) when path is stripped from combined_text. cmdi/path_traversal/ssrf/sqli/xss stayed strong (F1 >= 0.93) without path, showing they carry genuine payload-level signal, not just endpoint-matching. benign/idor did NOT hold up (idor precision 0.07, benign recall 0.31) - traced to a hard information collision, not undertraining: 1602/3809 rows (42%) share the identical stripped text '{} ' (empty query_params + empty body), comprising 1479 benign rows and all 123 idor rows. No model can separate identical input strings into different classes; IDOR is defined via a path segment (/basket/<id>) that literally does not exist in query_params/body. CONCLUSION: combined_text (with path) is the correct design - path is not an illegitimate shortcut, it is required information for IDOR specifically and contributes meaningfully elsewhere. REMAINING LIMITATION: cmdi and the path_traversal/ssrf classes tied to DVWA/Juice Shop's specific local endpoints (/vulnerabilities/exec/, /vulnerabilities/fi/, /profile/image/url) may not generalize to a different target app's endpoint layout, though payload-only signal (0.93-1.00 F1) suggests partial generalization is plausible. See scripts/ablation_cnn_payload_only.py for the diagnostic.

ablation_payload_only.description: Same architecture/split, trained on query_params+body only (path stripped)
